results.basis: Settled parts: the feat carries a printed action cost, so per principle E generalised (a reaction must appear in the reactions list; an action must appear as an action) it is listed at ⟨1⟩ with its text in the popup. The 15-foot range marker follows Ruling D as the owner applied it to Black Powder Boost — also an action-feat — 'Black Powder Boost show the +10 in (). with a * linking to the feat' on the Leap action; and the Athletics star follows Ruling C / principle D (star every skill that could perform the named action).
results.openQuestion: Two owner answers pull opposite ways for an ACTION-feat whose riders change a later basic action. Ruling D marked the Leap action for Black Powder Boost (an action-feat, numeric rider); the Minor Omen answer (#7) said an action-feat's own resolution can live entirely in its popup, 'there isnt a need for it to impact the sheet in another way'. Which governs Hydraulic Maneuvers' two NON-numeric riders — the item/body-bonus suppression and crit-failure-becomes-failure? Plausible answers: (a) all three riders ride in the marker on Disarm/Shove/Trip plus the Athletics star (Black Powder Boost shape); (b) only the numeric '15 feet' marks those actions, the two non-numeric riders stay in the feat's own popup (a split); (c) no markers at all — listing the feat as a ⟨1⟩ action with its text is the whole requirement (Minor Omen shape). Secondary, and needed whichever way (a) or (b) goes: is a one-check suppression of already-totalled item/circumstance bonuses something the sheet should ever be asked to express beyond printed prose?

requirements.clause: Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.

requirements.what: A jaws unarmed Strike on the strikes list: 1d8 piercing, brawling weapon group, unarmed trait, rolled with the character's own attack bonus and damage modifiers.
requirements.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait.

requirements.what: A 'deteriorated' state the player can switch on and off, applying Slowed 1 while it is on and carrying its full printed text. requirements.clause: the basic undead benefits → 'Disease and Poison Protection: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws (or any other defense) against disease and poison.'

requirements.what: From that package: undead vision — low-light vision, upgraded to darkvision if the character's ancestry already has low-light vision. The grant is conditional on the ancestry's existing sense.

requirements.what: From that package: the healing polarity is inverted — void/negative effects that heal undead restore your Hit Points and you take no void damage, while vitality/positive damage harms you and vitality healing does not help you. Nothing in the app expresses a flipped healing polarity; it is not a resistance, an immunity or a weakness.

This is a rewrite of how the Dying condition resolves for this character, so it marks the Dying condition — the shape the owner chose for The Survivor.
requirements.clause: the basic undead benefits → 'Negative Survival: … You are knocked out and begin dying when reduced to 0 Hit Points. … When you would die, you're destroyed rather than dead.'

results.basis: Settled parts, and by what: the all-Speeds penalty, the fist trait edit, the jaws strike and its usage note are lane-backed and 3/3-agreed (`speedPenalty`, `weaponRider`, `grantsStrike`, plus Ruling D/G for the note — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at). The deteriorated state is a mode carrying its full text (principle B), addressable by other zombie records (principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). The 10-minute repair is reachable at daily preparations, which Ruling K puts on the sheet rather than in the builder. Expanding the referenced Basic Undead Benefits package follows principle G (a granted feature needs its details surfaced), and its immunity / sense / language parts have lanes; its +1 vs disease and poison is Ruling B (a restricted flat bonus becomes a star).
results.openQuestion: Two clauses no principle reaches. (1) CREATURE TRAITS — 'You gain the undead and zombie traits.' Does the sheet have to record creature traits the character acquires, so that the player (and anything keyed to being undead) can see them? Plausible answers: (a) a trait line on the sheet listing acquired creature traits, treated as data other records can read; (b) display-only text on the granting record, no structured field; (c) nothing — the feat's description says it, the GM adjudicates. (2) THE UNDEAD BODY RULES — negative/void healing polarity (void heals you, vitality harms you) and negative survival (dying instead of destroyed at 0 HP). Ruling E says HP and damage never move sheet stats; does that also mean healing polarity gets no mechanical surface, or should it reach the HP/damage tooling and the defences panel (where resistances and immunities already live)? Plausible answers: (a) polarity is modelled where damage is applied, and Negative Survival becomes a marker on the Dying condition (The Survivor shape); (b) both stay as surfaced text on the granted Basic Undead Benefits entry only; (c) polarity is modelled, survival is text. A third, smaller item the owner may want to rule on at the same time: our record's immunities list (disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep) does not match the package's printed text and looks like a data defect rather than a requirement.

requirements.what: A named action, Bless Ally, appears in the character's actions and can be used from there, with its own cost and traits (⟨1⟩; concentrate, divine, fortune, mythic) and its details reachable. Only its existence is required here; performing it is the player's job.
requirements.clause: You gain the Bless Ally action.

requirements.what: A use pool of one per HOUR that the player can spend and watch refresh — an hourly period, not the usual per-day one.
requirements.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw

requirements.what: A `*` on the Will save carrying the fortune effect in words: once per hour you may roll twice and use the higher result. It adds no number, so the marker on the save is the whole surface — this is the shape the owner chose for the once-per-day Deception reroll in The Truth as I See it.
requirements.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw

requirements.what: A marker on the Confused condition itself: for this character it resolves as stubbornly immobile, wasting all actions until the condition ends, instead of attacking wildly. The condition is the thing the player is looking at when it matters.
requirements.clause: If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends.

requirements.what: A switchable nimbus state — on unless suppressed, suppressed or reestablished by a single action with the concentrate trait — carrying the full printed text: bright light in a 30-foot radius, dim light for another 30 feet, and, while it is active, a +1 status bonus to allies' saves against fear. It must be switchable because the rest of the feat is worded 'as long as your nimbus is active'. It changes none of the character's own numbers; the ally bonus produces no number on this sheet, but the player must be able to see that the ability is running and read what it gives.
requirements.clause: Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait. As long as your nimbus is active, all allies in the area of your nimbus gain a +1 status bonus to saves against fear.

results.basis: Settled parts, and by what: Bless Ally is a plain `grantsAction` (the shape of Unwavering Resilience, and the record already carries it); the once-per-hour pool is `limitedUses`; the Confused rewrite is Ruling D exactly as the owner applied it to The Survivor ('add a * on the dying condition linking to the feat') — a condition marker; and the Will fortune star follows gold answer #16, where a once-per-day roll-twice-take-better on a named roll became 'a * on deception' carrying the reroll, reinforced by Ruling H (stars go on the saves themselves, trigger printed). Minor Omen (#7) does not override that: there the whole feat was a reaction and the reaction listing carried the text, whereas this fortune effect is passive and has no action listing to live in.
results.openQuestion: The nimbus. Ruling F case 1 says an effect landing on a teammate puts NOTHING on your sheet, and case 2 grants the activator a display-only mode only when the effect 'is active to a limited amount of time'. The nimbus is ally-only AND permanent-until-suppressed, so it falls between them. Gold answer #3 ('we need to have a mode for Shield the Faithful') and the lanes manual (which names an aura as a `mode`) point to a mode; a literal reading of Ruling F case 1 points to nothing beyond the feat's own description. Exactly: does a permanent, player-suppressible, ally-only aura get a display-only mode carrying its full text, or no sheet surface at all? Plausible answers: (a) a display-only mode, default on, toggled by the single concentrate action, carrying the light radii and the allies' +1 vs fear — my listed requirement; (b) no mode, but a permanent star/marker on the feat's own record noting the light and that it can be suppressed (the Ruling M 'permanent star' shape for auras); (c) nothing — the description already says what allies get, and whether the light is lit is table fiction. Whichever way this goes it decides the other 39 aura records, so it is worth answering once.

Thievery is the only skill that can Pick a Lock, so it is the only skill starred. There is no number to add and no degree-of-success field in the app, so the printed sentence with its trigger is the surface.
requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.

requirements.what: The same upgrade marks the Pick a Lock action itself, with a `*` linking back to this feat — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters.
requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.

results.basis: Principle D / Ruling C decides the contested clause: the owner's Mastermind's Eye answer — 'i want the feat to have a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the use can see what happens when he cheks his recall knolladge number' — is the same shape, a passive feat whose effect fires off a named skill action and which carries no number. Here exactly one skill performs Pick a Lock, so Thievery alone is starred, and Ruling D puts the matching marker on the Pick a Lock action. The training grant and its already-trained redirect are the plain `skillTrained` + `redundantFallback` lanes, and principle K keeps the replacement-skill pick in the builder with no sheet control.
results.openQuestion: A feat upgrades YOUR OWN degree of success on one named skill action — Adroit Manipulation: "if you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead." (a) Is a printed star carrying that sentence the whole requirement, or does the app need a real degree-of-success field that actually computes the upgraded outcome? (This same clause covers 176 live records, currently prose-only inside a situational note's text.) (b) Does the clause get ONE mark or TWO — a `*` on the Thievery skill (as you asked for on every Recall Knowledge skill for Mastermind's Eye), a marker on the Pick a Lock action itself (as you asked for on Treat Wounds / Leap / the Dying condition under Ruling D), or both?
results.demotedBecause:
The confidence rests on Principle D / Ruling C, but that principle answers "which skills get starred when a bonus is named after an action" — a question that is not contested here, because the feat's own text names the skill ("a Thievery check to Pick a Lock"). The principle does no work on the only genuinely contested point.

What the three readers actually split on (1/3 note, 1/3 situational, 1/3 "none fits") is whether a DEGREE-OF-SUCCESS upgrade is discharged by a printed marker at all. Nothing in the gold set or the rulings addresses that. Verified: work/rulings/DECISIONS.md and DECISIONS-round2.md contain no ruling on "success becomes critical success" (the word "critical" does not appear in round 2 at all). The project's own record (project_hh_lane_gap_diff) lists AdjustDegreeOfSuccess as one of nine systems with NO route in the app — 176 records, types.ts has no degree field, ~116 already sitting as display-only prose inside a situational note's `bonus` string. The gold set deliberately placed #29 in the "missing-system" stratum for exactly this clause, and the owner's round-1 answers (#1,2,3,6,7,8,9,13,15,16) skipped every feat in that stratum. So the reviewer's "there is no degree-of-success field in the app, so the printed sentence is the surface" ratifies the status quo as correct — a scope decision on an unmodelled system, not a principle application. Foundry, the corroborating implementation, models this with AdjustDegreeOfSuccess, i.e. treats it as a real mechanic rather than prose.

Second, independent problem: the call applies Principle D and Ruling D simultaneously, producing TWO surfaces for one sentence, and Ruling D's antecedent is not met. Ruling D is titled "Bonuses with no stat row (32 records)" and its shape is "show the changed value inline in parentheses, with a * linking to the source" — here there IS a stat row (Thievery) and there is NO value, so it fails twice. The owner explicitly REJECTED "star the nearest roll" as the alternative to marking the thing modified, and Ruling G states the mark lives on the one thing you are looking at and that an upgrade "REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it." The claimed same-shape precedent cuts the same way: for Mastermind's Eye the owner asked for a star on every Recall Knowledge skill and NO mark on the Recall Knowledge action. So requirement 5 departs from the very precedent invoked to justify requirement 4. Two reasonable builders plainly disagree — star Thievery only, mark Pick a Lock only, or both.

Minor third point: "Thievery is the only skill that can Pick a Lock" is asserted flatly, but the app has a skillSubstitution lane and Ruling H says where the rules are open, stay open. Not decisive on its own, but it is another silent narrowing.

Requirements 1-3 (skillTrained, redundantFallback, builder-only choice under K) are uncontroversial and 3/3-agreed. The confidence is carried entirely by requirements 4 and 5, and it stretches Ruling D from a placement rule into an existence rule. The identical clause appears three times in the 43-feat gold set (#29, #30, #34) and 176 times live, so a wrong entry here propagates at scale — exactly the case the default-to-demote rule covers.

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus that applies only to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait. Because the rules restrict it, it sits outside the flat Will total as a starred conditional entry with 'against effects with the emotion trait' as its trigger.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait

requirements.what: A second marker, wider than the first: on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect — Fortitude, Reflex and Will, not just Will — a success becomes a critical success. All three saves are starred with the printed trigger, because the text names no single save and narrowing it would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's. It adds no number, so the sentence itself is the surface; the app has no degree-of-success field and carries such clauses as prose on the save's entry.
requirements.clause: and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead

requirements.what: The two entries have different triggers (Will-only versus any save), so both must be visible rather than one collapsing into the other.
requirements.clause: a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait, and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect…

results.basis: Ruling B decides the bonus — 'Move it to a star': a flat bonus the rules restrict leaves the stat total and becomes a situational entry with the restriction in its `when`. Ruling H decides the scope of the second clause — 'keep it open. Star all saves, and the note says … You decide at the table' (Bootstrap Respirator), so the crit-upgrade stars every save with the printed trigger rather than being narrowed to Will. That the non-numeric upgrade earns a star at all is settled by principle D / the Mastermind's Eye answer: a passive feat whose effect fires off one of your own checks is starred where the player looks up that number. Placement on the saves is Ruling D / principle J (the mark goes on the specific thing affected), and the cross-cutting stacking ruling ('show both if the string doesn't match') keeps both entries visible.
results.openQuestion: When a passive feat upgrades the degree of success on one of YOUR OWN saving throws and adds no number, does it get its own starred entry on the save rows — and on all three saves when the clause names no single save? You told us Minor Omen's save-side reroll needed no surface beyond the reactions list ("there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way"), yet Adhyabhau's crit-upgrade is the same kind of non-computable, self-roll clause. If it does get a star, confirm the two-line result on the Will row is what you want: "+1 circumstance from Adhyabhau — against emotion effects" sitting directly above "a success is a critical success instead from Adhyabhau — against an emotion effect", since the Will-only bonus and the all-saves upgrade cannot be folded into one entry without either losing Fortitude and Reflex or leaking the +1 onto them.
results.demotedBecause:
Demote. The requirements are probably right on the merits, but not one of the four cited principles actually reaches the contested clause, and an on-point owner precedent inside the reviewer's own source document was dropped.

1) DROPPED PRECEDENT, in the very file being cited. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/docs/gold-set-answers.md line 67 glosses the owner's Minor Omen answer as "Nothing else — explicitly not a degree-of-success surface." That is the only owner statement in the whole corpus touching a non-numeric clause that changes how one of YOUR OWN saving throws resolves, and it declined the save-side surface. The reviewer cites Mastermind's Eye from the same file and never mentions Minor Omen. Minor Omen is distinguishable (it is a reaction, so it already has a surface; a reroll is not a degree step) — but that distinction is the reviewer's judgment, not anything the owner said. Grep confirms no owner ruling on degree-of-success exists anywhere in work/rulings/DECISIONS.md or DECISIONS-round2.md.

2) PRINCIPLE D IS A SCOPE RULE USED AS AN EXISTENCE RULE. The owner's Mastermind's Eye words ("a * in every skill that can recall knolladge") and DECISIONS.md Ruling C ("Star every skill that could do it") both answer WHICH rows get a star, presupposing one is warranted. Neither says a non-computable clause earns a star at all. And gold-set-review.md:119 flags Mastermind's Eye as CONTROL VIOLATED with readers SPLIT — the owner had to be asked. Using the case that required an owner ruling as the principle that decides a different shape outright is the stretch.

3) RULING H'S PRECONDITION IS NOT MET. DECISIONS.md:232 reads "WHERE THE RULES ARE OPEN, STAY OPEN"; its example, Bootstrap Respirator ("saves that require you to smell or taste"), names no save at all. Adhyabhau says "a saving throw" immediately after saying "Will saves" — so the live question is whether that shift is deliberate widening or elliptical continuation. That is a reading dispute, not the silence H addresses. H may reach it by analogy; it does not decide it. H.2's "cap the note at about one line" is also not met by requirement 2's two-sentence framing.

4) THE STACKING BASIS IS FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT THE MACHINERY. poolSituationalLines (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3406) keys on parseBonus type + normalizeWhen(l.when); the target save is not in the key. On the Will row the two entries' `when` strings are near-identical, so "different triggers (Will-only versus any save)" is not what separates them. What actually keeps both visible is parseBonus returning null for a non-numeric bonus, so keyOf returns null and the line never pools. Requirement 3 survives — the real reason is that the scope split (will vs all) makes a single entry impossible without either losing Fort/Ref or leaking the +1 onto them — but the cited cross-cutting ruling is not what decides it.

5) THE STRATUM AND THE SHIPPED CODE BOTH SAY THIS IS UNSETTLED. scripts/audit/gold-answer-key.json files feat 30 as "stratum": "missing-system" and marks all three second-clause proposals agreedBy:1, confidence:"low", split three ways on the lane (note / situational / null). The reviewer's list contains no "no lane fits" entry, which forecloses the finding mechanic-lanes.md calls the most valuable bucket there is; project_hh_lane_gap_diff lists AdjustDegreeOfSuccess as one of nine systems with NO route (176 records, types.ts has no degree field). Whether prose-in-a-star is the requirement or merely today's workaround has never been put to the owner.

Fairness: requirement 1 is safe — Ruling B plus the shipped src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:100, which already carries exactly {kind:'save',detail:'will'}, when "against emotion effects", bonus "+1 circumstance". And there is house style for the second clause standing alone: irrepressible / -ganzi / -halfling / -nephilim (:2740-2743) and cantorian-reinforcement (:2700) all use save:'all' + "a success is a critical success instead".

But for THIS shape — a numeric restricted bonus AND a degree upgrade on the same trigger family — the app has two live records and both ship the number only: adhyabhau (:100) and divine-health (:180, its own "success becomes a critical success" clause absent). So requirements 2 and 3 change house behaviour on a two-record shape with no owner ruling behind them. That is exactly the propagation risk the gate exists to catch.

results.basis: Partly decided. Ruling F plus Principle B settle the ally half: the +1 that allies in the emanation get puts no number on your sheet, but Bless's own text must stay readable so the player knows what is running. Ruling D/G put the rank and radius notes on the granted effect rather than loose on the feat. What is NOT decided is the shape of your OWN +1, and that is the whole substance of the feat.
results.openQuestion: This is the first case in the set of 'a spell is permanently running on you', and two calls are needed. (a) Where does your own +1 status bonus to attack rolls live? Ruling M's decided aura shape is a permanent star carrying the positional condition in its note, and it says in terms 'not a mode' — but Ruling M was answering 'am I standing inside this emanation?', a question that cannot arise here, because the emanation is centred on you and you are always in it, so nothing restricts the bonus. Plausible answers: (i) a real +1 status bonus inside the attack totals, since Ruling B sends only RESTRICTED bonuses to situational and this one is unrestricted; (ii) a permanent star on attack rolls per Ruling M, so every aura in the app keeps one shape; (iii) a mode that is on by default and carries the +1, which is what Dismiss argues for. (b) Is the effect modelled by copying Bless's numbers onto this feat, or by representing 'the Bless spell is running on you' as a state that points at the Bless record — so its description, its half-your-level rank and its Dismiss/return behaviour hang off the spell instead of being restated on the feat? The owner's answer to #3 built a mode for an aura, which points at (iii) plus the state; Ruling M points at (ii) plus copying. Nothing in the answers reaches an always-on self-affecting instance of another record.

requirements.what: Your own attack rolls must carry the Bless +1 status bonus, permanently. The emanation is centred on you, so unlike a normal aura there is no positional condition to state — you are never outside it. Whether that lands in the attack total or as a permanent star is the open question.
requirements.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell, with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up).

requirements.what: The Bless effect must be visible as something permanently running on the character, carrying Bless's own full text — including the part that benefits allies, which moves no number of yours but which the player still has to be able to read.
requirements.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell, with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up).

requirements.what: The effect must be switchable off and back on: Dismissing it suppresses the bonus, and it comes back on its own after 1 minute. Duration is not tracked, so the return is text, but the off state has to be reachable.
requirements.clause: You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.

requirements.what: The effect's spell rank must be shown and must be derived from level (half your level, rounded up), re-derived at every level-up rather than stored as a literal the way granted-spell ranks normally are. It moves none of your numbers; it matters for counteracting.
requirements.clause: with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up)

requirements.what: The fixed 15-foot radius must be printed on the granted effect, and it must override Bless's own area growth — this feat forbids increasing it. That is a change to a parameter of the very thing the feat supplies, so it belongs on the granted effect, not on the feat in isolation.
requirements.clause: The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it.

results.basis: Ruling B decides the first two: a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, sitting outside the stat total — that is correct, not a defect. Ruling D/G decides the third: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and the thing here is the initiative roll itself, not Perception and not any one skill (the app already carries initiative as its own statistic that reads whatever stat you roll it with, so `{kind:'initiative'}` is the home, and filing it under Perception would silently drop it for a character who rolls Stealth or Deception). Ruling G decides the fourth: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so the +4 supersedes the +1 instead of adding to it. The confidence rests on a load-bearing factual claim that the code refutes — "Nothing here needs a new system" — and it is false twice over.

(1) Principle C is stretched past its source AND has no surface here. C came from #3, where the modified thing was a MODE, an object that carries text and can visibly show a modification. Requirement 1 demands the mark land on Ancient Memories, a passive ancestry feat (`actionCost.type: 'passive'`). The `modifiesGrant` lane has exactly three shapes (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\types.ts:754-770): `innateUsesPerDay`, `actionRider`, `deityDomainsFromChoice`. Only `actionRider` displays anything, and build.ts:3427-3436 turns it into a `RecordMarker` whose `on` is typed `'action' | 'condition'` (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts:3167-3177). There is no marker route onto a feat row. So the one requirement the reviewer called decided by an owner principle is the one the app cannot express.

(2) The visibility C exists to secure is already delivered without it. `dailyChoicesFor` emits a row carrying `recordName` (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\dailyChoices.ts:19-30, 35-60), so at rest the player sees "Ancient Memories — …" and "Endless Memories — …" adjacent. Healing Sanctuary had nowhere else for its text to go; this feat does. A second reasonable builder would say C is satisfied by construction and a marker on Ancient Memories is duplication. That alone is the demotion test.

(3) Requirement 1's own premise contradicts requirement 3. "The feat has no standalone effect" is not true of the printed text — it grants a temporary expert rank in a skill of the player's choosing, a number on the player's own sheet, which the reviewer asserts two requirements later. If it has a standalone effect the `modifiesGrant` classification loses its basis.

(4) Principle K is invoked to justify a surface K denies. K reads "Anything the player re-chooses in the builder needs no sheet surface", and its source (#15 Guerrilla Dedication) is an owner answer that asked for nothing. Requirement 5 cites K and then demands a `note` — a real lane (mechanic-lanes.md §J). Applied faithfully K yields zero requirements for the retrain clause. The shapes also differ: Guerrilla's builder re-pick is re-choosing that feat's own field; here the retrain is a permanent skill-increase change constrained by two stored daily flags the app already holds, so "nothing computes" is a choice, not a consequence.

(5) Ruling D is cited for something that is not a DC. D's sentence is "a skill DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers". Generalising "the player remembers" to a retrain restriction is an extension the owner never made.

(6) "Nothing needs a new system" fails a second time on requirement 2's Lore clause. `kind: 'array'` options are static; `effectiveChoiceOptions` (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\derive.ts:997-1022) only merges other records' static `choiceOptionAdditions`; and `OpenChoiceFrom.type` (types.ts:1055) is spell|feat|weapon|language|heritage|own-spell|own-feat|own-item|own-companion — there is no skill or lore source. `dailyChoiceGrants` (derive.ts:1072-1075) converts an `open` answer into a grant only for `from.type === 'spell'`, so even a hypothetical skill picker would grant nothing. The live record's own note concedes it: "Lore skills are not enumerable here." `requiresSkillRank` does support `min` (types.ts:1372), so the 16 enumerable skills are fine — the Lore half is not.

(7) Two clauses were silently dropped. (a) The second pick is conditional: "*When* you choose a skill … with Ancient Memories, you *can also* choose…". Nothing in dailyChoices.ts can gate one daily choice on another being answered, and Ancient Memories' choice is `kind: 'skills'`, which dailyChoices.ts:41-42 skips outright — the antecedent is never even offered. (b) "already trained" as of when? `qualifiesForOption` (derive.ts:1037-1046) reads `c.proficiencies.skills`, the BUILD ranks, so this morning's Ancient Memories grant would not qualify a skill. That may be right RAW, but it falls out of an implementation detail; the opposite reading is defensible, and the requirement says only "the character's current ranks" without saying which.

(8) A lane-key mismatch that would propagate. mechanic-lanes.md defines `rankUpgrade` as "At Nth level you become master/legendary in X", satisfied by `featGrantsAuto.rankUpgrade` — a `{level, rank}` step against an already-named skill (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\featGrantsAuto.ts:21,114,336). This feat's mechanism is `choice.options[].grant.skills` read by `dailySkillRank`, which the manual calls `effectGrant` under `dailyChoice`. The reviewer used `rankUpgrade` off-label and admitted the mismatch in prose. A presence-comparison script would look for `featGrantsAuto.rankUpgrade`, find nothing, and file a false defect against a correctly-built record — across 6,179 feats that is precisely the propagation the demotion rule guards against.

The reviewer's two DEFECT observations are correct and I verified them: endless-memories has 0/16 options carrying a `grant` and 0 carrying `requiresSkillRank`, and ancient-memories' `kind: 'skills'` is skipped by dailyChoicesFor. Being right about the defects does not rescue the confidence — the spec questions above are untouched by them.
